definitions.explanation: The act of yawning, typically from sleepiness, boredom, or fatigue. The noun あくび (yawn) takes the particle を with する.

examples.japanese: ⟦{授業中|じゅぎょうちゅう}→授業中：20544_jugyouchuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧あくびをしてしまった。
⟦{退屈|たいくつ}→退屈：03389_taikutsu⟧な⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}ていて→見る：00283_miru⟧、⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧あくびをした。
examples.english: I yawned many times while watching a boring movie.

examples.japanese: ⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧あくびをしたら、つられてあくび⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧しまうこと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: When the person next to you yawns, you sometimes end up yawning too.

notes:
The standard way to say "to yawn" in Japanese. The noun あくび can also be written in kanji as ⟦{欠伸|あくび}→欠伸：06484_akubi⟧, though the hiragana form is far more common in modern usage.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- あくびをする — to yawn (basic form)
- あくび⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧ — a yawn comes out (involuntary feeling)
- あくび⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{噛|か}み{殺|ころ}す→噛み殺す：29106_kamikorosu⟧ — to stifle a yawn

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧あくび — a big yawn
- あくび⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{止|と}まらない→止まる：00555_tomaru⟧ — can't stop yawning
- あくび⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{我慢|がまん}する→我慢する：25343_gamansuru⟧ — to hold back a yawn
- あくび⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧うつる — yawning is contagious

CULTURAL NOTE:
Yawning in public is generally considered rude in Japan, especially in formal settings. It is common practice to cover one's mouth with a hand when yawning. In business meetings or school, visible yawning may be taken as a sign of disrespect or lack of interest.
